outcome: Website components render on white unless the organiser sets another colour.

name: Larger system messages

name: Card border and shadow

name: Component internal names

outcome: Users only see tour steps relevant to their event, worded in the event's own terms.

why: DWTC asked for these; the request does not state the reason.
outcome: Organisers build and run more of their marketing site inside the website builder.
builtOverlap: Related: EP-8831 gallery with search, upload and folders; the auto-sync, naming and bulk upload asks are not covered [MASTER Event Website §5 User Stories Mapping :5929]

outcome: Organisers keep exhibitor tag filters current and in the order they want.

name: Parent sessions kept off child exhibitor profiles
what: Change the 'We speak at' block on a child exhibitor's profile (web and app) so it no longer shows the parent exhibitor's sessions.

name: Keep parent team members out of child messages

name: Products visible only via QR code

name: Team members hidden from unregistered visitors

name: Hide location in the exhibitor list
what: The title asks to hide the location shown in the exhibitor list; every other field says "Jonathan please add".
why: Not stated in the request.

name: Thumbnails for Word and Excel marketing content
what: Generate thumbnails for .docx and .xlsx marketing content as for PDFs, or allow a default image when a thumbnail is missing.

outcome: All marketing content cards show a thumbnail.

name: Product statistics on the team member dashboard
what: Show total products, total product favourites and total product views on the team member admin dashboard, as the exhibitor profile dashboard already does.
why: Only the exhibitor sees actions taken on its products; the organiser (Vinexposium) wants team member admins to see the same numbers. The request calls it good to have.

outcome: Exhibitors track which invitees completed registration.
builtOverlap: Partially built: statistics for the invited visitors flow (EP-27290) [MASTER Online Registration §5 User Stories Mapping :5318]

name: Category auto-assigned from answers
what: Extend registration pipeline conditional logic (visitor and exhibitor) so a specific answer to a question, e.g. "main activity" = importer, automatically sets the participant category (e.g. buyer) while the category field stays hidden.
why: Vinexpo India can only show or hide the category field by condition, so records get the default category and must be updated by hand. Asked by Vinexposium (T1).
outcome: Registrants get the right category from their answers, and their e-badge shows it, with no manual updates.
builtOverlap: Related: default category auto-assigned when none is selected; answer-based assignment is the ask (EP-14938) [MASTER Online Registration §5 User Stories Mapping :5298]

name: Separate T&Cs per registration pipeline
what: Configure separate Terms & Conditions for the participant (person) and exhibitor (company) registration pipelines.
why: DLG: every other registration setting is separate per pipeline but Terms is shared, so everyone passes through all T&Cs; the workaround is an extra pipeline step. Asked by DLG Markets GmbH (T1).
outcome: Visitors and exhibitors see only the T&Cs that apply to them.

name: Multiple categories on one profile
what: Add an event-level option for multiple participant categories on one profile: an API/import update with the same ID, external ID, email and name but a new category adds that category, while the same email with a different name creates a fake-email profile; the latest category's permissions apply, all external QR codes log into the same account, the user picks which badge to print or show, and leads stay with the profile.
why: VIPs and government delegates who are also speakers or exhibitors get separate profiles with fake emails, and shared government emails are used for several people, so meetings are lost and leads go missing from exhibitor files; DWTC and the EP team handle many such cases. Asked by Dubai World Trade Centre DWTC/ DXB Live (T1).
outcome: Each attendee has one profile holding all their roles, badges and codes, and meetings and leads stay attached to it.
builtOverlap: Related: visual flag on fake-email accounts; does not merge categories into one profile (EP-12726) [MASTER User Engagement §5 User Stories Mapping :9994]

name: Explain incomplete-profile redirect

outcome: Users know they must complete their profile before reaching the meeting.

name: External ticketing for visitor registration
what: Support visitor registration through an external ticketing system; the request has a title only.
why: Not stated in the request. Asked by Frankfurter Buchmesse GmbH (T1), Adventics.
outcome: Not stated beyond the title.

name: Multiple scan-in check-in mode
what: Offer a multiple scan-in option in onsite check-in instead of paired scan-in and scan-out.
why: Kortrijk wants to record when people enter without scanning them out, as there is no capacity to do so.
outcome: Staff record each entry without having to scan exits.
builtOverlap: Related (EP-23669): Check-in App settings rework; the KB notes the app already records repeated check-ins separately and check-out needs an explicit mode switch (Onsite & Kiosks :3591) [MASTER Mobile App §5 User Stories Mapping :10647] via EP-273

name: Printed badge QR code size
what: Let organisers customise the size of the QR code on the printed badge.
why: Informa Healthcare reports that at Pharmapack the QR code on physical badges was too small to scan.
outcome: Printed badge QR codes are large enough to scan reliably.

name: Separate QR code and barcode placement on badges
what: Let the QR code and barcode be positioned separately on both the printed and the digital badge.
why: On the print badge they sit side by side and look cramped; on the digital badge the barcode is locked under the QR code, making both harder to scan. Tier 1 customers asking: Informa Markets (UK).
outcome: Organisers lay out QR code and barcode separately and badges scan more easily.
builtOverlap: Related (EP-9822): size control for QR and barcode fields, not separate placement [MASTER Onsite & Kiosks §5 User Stories Mapping :3767] via EP-6549

name: Audible check-in confirmation
what: Play an audible signal on the scanning device when a check-in is accepted.
why: Requested by Kortrijk Xpo.
outcome: Staff hear confirmation of each accepted check-in without looking at the screen.

name: Bulk removal of external QR codes
what: Let organisers bulk-remove all external QR codes for an event themselves.
why: Reusing external QR strings across events mixes up data, and cleaning them today needs a developer database operation that is no longer acceptable; raised for IMEX Frankfurt and IMEX America 2026. Comments ask where the codes and the button live in the admin panel.
outcome: Organisers clear an event's external QR codes without developer help.
builtOverlap: Related (EP-10400): history of external QR codes is stored; no bulk removal [MASTER Onsite & Kiosks §5 User Stories Mapping :3768] via FIS-1763672070

name: Tab and page click analytics
what: Give the show team backend analytics on how many times each tab or page is clicked in the app and on the website.
why: Informa's Smart Events team wants to see the usage rate of each tab for pre- and post-event analysis; a comment notes the ask is ambiguous and not needed for Pharmapack and CPHI.
outcome: Organisers see which pages and tabs attendees use most.
builtOverlap: Partially built (EP-20705): The mobile analytics page reports page views by page type; per-tab website clicks are not covered [MASTER Organiser Analytics §5 User Stories Mapping :2764]; Related (EP-1127): page visits and views collected on the new UI [MASTER Organiser Analytics §5 User Stories Mapping :2758]

name: Trending product categories
what: Rank product categories by how often visitors search or view them, via marketplace filters, header search and category pages.
why: Qmed wants organisers to know which categories are trending with the audience, as its previous directory reported. Tier 1 asking: Informa Markets (UK).
outcome: Organisers see which product categories visitors look for most.

name: Sent email content audit
what: Store the content of every sent email, including rendered variables, for 18 months, and add a "See email content" action in Analytics → Email track that shows it in a popup (plain text as MVP; images and attachments optional).
why: Hyve admins need to check exactly what a user received when a dispute arises, for example a complaint about inappropriate content.
outcome: Admins open any sent email from the email tracking list and see what the recipient received.

name: Event time zone for all export times
what: Show all times inside exported reports, including participant registration (creation) time and profile completed time, in the event location's time zone, formatted YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS with the UTC offset in 24-hour time.
why: Frankfurter Buchmesse sees that export links already follow the event location time (EP-29932), but creation and profile completion times in the files are still GMT, so reporting times are inconsistent.
outcome: Every time in every report is in the event's local time with a consistent format.
builtOverlap: Partially built: exports already show the timezone per the event's country setting; creation and completion fields are the gap [MASTER Admin / Platform Core §4 Feature Inventory :1313 Data Export]

name: Exhibitor events export with attendees
what: Add an "Export Event Data" button under Data > Import/Export that produces an XLS of all exhibitor events (name, date, time, location, description, speaker, moderator) with a column of the full names of users who added each event to their schedule.
why: Exhibitors want to track engagement with their events and follow up with the attendees who scheduled them. Tier 1 asking: IMEX.
outcome: Organisers download one file listing every exhibitor event and who scheduled it.
builtOverlap: Related (EP-36095): attendee names column exists in the team schedule export [MASTER Sessions & Speakers §5 User Stories Mapping :8711]; Related (EP-24160): exhibitor event date/time is in the leads export [MASTER Lead Intelligence §5 User Stories Mapping :12741]

name: Attend a Stand report
what: Add an Attend a Stand export under Admin panel > Data > Import/Export > Export with one row per request, the specified columns, all exhibitor stands as hall_name: stand_name, and the request creation timestamp.
why: Hyve needs the Attend a Stand requests as a report; the work was planned for an earlier event and postponed.
outcome: Organisers can download every Attend a Stand request with stand and timestamp details.

name: Video on person profiles
what: Add the exhibitor profile's video and additional video fields to visitor and team member profiles.
why: Informa wants it for the Distributor Hub community of Informa Healthcare (Omnia Health).
outcome: Visitors and team members show a video on their profile.

name: URL field https auto-completion
what: Automatically add "https://" to a URL typed without a protocol when the user finishes typing or presses Enter, without overriding "http://" or another protocol the user typed.
why: DLG Markets says this common practice saves time, reduces input errors and ensures URLs are properly formatted.
outcome: URLs users enter are saved correctly formatted without typing the protocol.

name: Country on search result cards
what: Show the country under the company name on producer/exhibitor search result cards and under position/company on participant cards.
why: Comexposium (Vinexposium, Vinexpo Community) runs an international community and wants the country visible.
outcome: Search cards show each person's and company's country.
builtOverlap: Related (EP-23519): company name and job title added to user cards [MASTER Networking & Interactions §5 User Stories Mapping :6834]

name: Featured sessions at the top of the list
what: Show featured sessions at the top of the sessions page with a 'featured' label, on web and in the app.
why: Not stated in the request.
outcome: Attendees see featured sessions first, clearly labelled.
builtOverlap: Related (EP-2672, EP-22334): website sessions block can filter by featured [MASTER Event Website §5 User Stories Mapping :5949]

name: Breakout rooms under a webinar
what: Let organisers create several breakout rooms under one main webinar session and push participants into them, as Zoom does.
why: Saladplate wants better group engagement; there is no main room linked to breakout rooms.
outcome: Participants move from a main webinar into smaller breakout groups.

name: Save button at the top of the session edit page
what: Move Save and Cancel to the top of the session edit page, or add autosave.
why: Organisers must scroll past images, settings, descriptions, speakers and attendees to save.
outcome: Organisers save session edits without scrolling.

name: Google Maps link for session location
what: Add a Google Maps link to the session card.
why: Adventics / Frankfurter Buchmesse: sessions and events take place in locations other than the venue, and attendees need to see where.
outcome: Attendees open the session location in Google Maps from the session card.
builtOverlap: Related (EP-11578, EP-24407): app shows the address for sessions in an "Other location"; no map link [MASTER Mobile App §5 User Stories Mapping :10650]

name: File attachments on sessions (web and app)
what: Let organisers attach files (up to at least 100 MB) to live sessions and show them on the session page on web and app, as for exhibitor profiles.
why: DWTC: sessions need content attached.
outcome: Attendees download session materials from the session page.

what: Add an "Attendance limit" setting per exhibitor event type (default "set by Exhibitor", or a fixed limit that presets and locks the exhibitor's input), and show remaining places on exhibitor event cards and pages on web and app, disabling Book when full.

outcome: Visitors in the chosen categories do not see the hidden track or its sessions.
builtOverlap: Partially built (EP-24229): session-level visibility restriction exists; track-level hiding per category is not documented [MASTER Sessions & Speakers §4 Feature Inventory :8651]

name: Highlighted note on sessions (multilingual)
what: Add a note text field to sessions, in each language for bilingual sessions, shown on the frontend to highlight specific information.
why: Vinexposium wants to highlight information many attendees miss in the description; CSS cannot target specific sessions and not all sessions are bilingual.
outcome: Attendees see a highlighted note on the sessions that need one, in their language.

name: Colour picker for session tracks
what: Replace the predefined colour set for session tracks with a colour picker that accepts any colour via hex, RGB or a visual spectrum.
why: Track colours are limited to a predefined palette, so Frankfurter Buchmesse and other organisers cannot match their brand colours.
outcome: Organisers give each track an exact brand colour, and tracks show that colour on session cards.

name: Localised language list in exhibitor event form
what: Show the language list in the exhibitor event submission form in the user's interface language (e.g. 'Deutsch' instead of 'German'), or as ISO-2 codes, on web and app.
why: Exhibitors submitting an exhibitor event in the German interface see the language list in English (Frankfurter Buchmesse).
outcome: Exhibitors see language names in the same language as the rest of the interface.

name: Consent gate for embedded session videos
what: Block iframe embeds in livestream and on-demand sessions and exhibitor events behind a consent banner until consent is given, on the session or exhibitor event page and in list and card views, or on the pre-entrance page, as done for exhibitor profile videos (EP-32016).
why: Consent must cover all end-user and exhibitor input where iframes are available, and online session embeds are not covered (Frankfurter Buchmesse).
outcome: Session video embeds load only after the viewer gives consent.

name: Questionnaire changes in exhibitor event change log
what: Show changes to the exhibitor event questionnaire answers (questions populated from marketing forms) in the admin 'View changes' for an edited exhibitor event, like other submission changes.
why: Exhibitors can change their questionnaire answers when editing an event, but organisers at Frankfurter Buchmesse cannot see those changes.
outcome: Organisers review every change to an exhibitor event, including questionnaire answers, before approving it.
builtOverlap: Related (EP-34350, EP-26093): organiser sets questions for exhibitors at submission; answer changes not shown [MASTER Sessions & Speakers §5 User Stories Mapping :8707]

name: Registration form for exhibitor events
what: Allow a registration form on exhibitor events, as already available for sessions, on web and app, with answers stored in the form.
why: Not stated in the request beyond DLG wanting the same option as for sessions.
outcome: Attendees register for exhibitor events through a form, and exhibitors and organisers get their answers.

name: Exhibitors add speakers to their events
what: Let exhibitors select speakers for their exhibitor events on the frontend (Exhibitor events > Edit), including creating new speaker accounts by email, name and surname, similar to adding team members.
why: Exhibitors cannot create speaker profiles, so Vinexposium has to collect speaker details and create them in the admin panel, which is manual work.
outcome: Exhibitors attach their own speakers to exhibitor events without organiser intervention.

name: Speaker preferred language for emails
what: Add a required preferred language field to the speaker creation dialogue in the admin panel and send the speaker's activation email in that language.
why: Speakers created in the admin panel always get the activation email in English, whatever the event's default language (DLG).
outcome: Speakers receive their activation email in their own language.

name: Open speaker profile directly from session pop-up
what: When a user clicks a co-speaker or moderator in a session pop-up, close the pop-up and open that person's profile directly.
why: Clicking another speaker leaves the session pop-up open and hides the profile behind it, which confuses DLG's attendees.
outcome: Attendees go straight from a session pop-up to the chosen speaker or moderator profile with no overlapping pop-ups.

name: Remove speakers without losing list page
what: Keep the admin on the current page of the speakers or moderators list after removing one, refreshing the list in place.
why: Removing a speaker or moderator sends the admin back to the first page, and with more than 100 speakers over several pages DLG admins lose their place.
outcome: Admins remove speakers or moderators one after another without losing their page in the list.
builtOverlap: Related (EP-46707, EP-27790): search in speaker/moderator lists for large datasets; removal behaviour unchanged [MASTER Sessions & Speakers §5 User Stories Mapping :8710]

name: Localised date formats in email templates
what: Format the date variable in session and meeting notification and reminder email templates by the event's country (US MM/DD/YYYY, Europe DD.MM.YYYY, Japan/China/Korea YYYY/MM/DD, India DD-MM-YYYY) instead of the fixed ISO YYYY-MM-DD.
why: The ISO format is unfamiliar to participants in some regions and can be misread; raised for DLG.
outcome: Participants receive notification emails with dates written in the format they know from their region.

name: Admin schedule download as PDF
what: Let admins download a user's schedule as PDF from the Admin Panel in addition to the Excel format.
why: IMEX: when Excel is chosen, the Admin Panel only offers Excel, so staff on site need five or six clicks through Customer Service login on the frontend to get a PDF some clients prefer.
outcome: Admins export a user's schedule as PDF or Excel directly from the Admin Panel.
builtOverlap: Related (EP-23040, EP-20775): My Schedule download in XLS (and PDF) on the frontend; admin PDF is not covered [MASTER Sessions & Speakers §5 User Stories Mapping :8700]

name: Exhibitor event attendance from badge scan
what: Extend how users get the Attended mark for exhibitor events: keep check-in app and manual admin marking (on a new Attendees tab), and add attendance when the owning exhibitor scans the badge of a user who has the event in their schedule during the event time plus or minus one hour; external check-ins are marked and locked, manual marks can be undone.
why: Organisers are unlikely to send staff to check in every exhibitor event or give exhibitors the check-in app, so exhibitor event attendance goes unrecorded.
outcome: Exhibitor event attendance is recorded from exhibitors' own badge scans and visible to organisers.
builtOverlap: Related (EP-39837, EP-11165): booked and attended session columns exist in the exhibitor sponsor dashboard [MASTER Onsite & Kiosks §5 User Stories Mapping :3770]

name: Linked exhibitor events applied together
what: Let exhibitors link exhibitor events into one group from the create/edit panel so applying to any event in the group applies to all of them; each event belongs to one group and the event page shows that applying means attending all linked events.
why: Not stated in the request.
outcome: Users apply once to a series of linked exhibitor events.

name: Retire old exhibitor event autoapproval
what: Remove Final Application Date, Final Application Time and Auto-approve Pending Applications After Deadline from exhibitor event create/edit, keeping the approval setting.
why: The epic introduces a new autoapproval mechanism for exhibitor events that replaces these fields.
outcome: Organisers configure exhibitor event approval only through the new mechanism.
builtOverlap: Related (EP-46200, EP-46110): the new autoapproval mechanism is delivered [MASTER Sessions & Speakers §5 User Stories Mapping :8715]; Related (EP-46200, EP-23521): per-type autoapproval of exhibitor events exists [MASTER Sessions & Speakers §5 User Stories Mapping :8702]

name: Speaker highlight border on all pages
what: Let organisers set a speaker border colour (e.g. a golden ring) that highlights speakers on all attendee-facing system pages and in the event app, not only in the website builder Speaker Block.
why: Vinexposium asked for it; today it is possible only in the website builder, so system pages and the app need custom CSS per event, which needs technical help and does not scale.
outcome: Speakers are visibly highlighted with the organiser's chosen border on system pages and in the app without custom CSS.
builtOverlap: Related (FIS-1400111125, EP-21632): website builder Speakers block exists; system pages and app are not covered [MASTER Event Website §5 User Stories Mapping :5944]

name: Sponsor visibility on the floor plan
what: Show sponsored exhibitors' logos and profile links highlighted on the interactive floor plan, and let sponsored exhibitors place banners on the floor plan.
why: Informa's Smart Events team has no way to highlight sponsors on the floor plan, which limits sponsored exhibitors' reach.
outcome: Sponsored exhibitors stand out on the floor plan and carry their own banners there.
builtOverlap: Partially built: Sponsor banners on the global and hall pages of the new UI floor plan exist; highlighted sponsor logos on stands are not covered (EP-8019, via EP-1675) [MASTER Sponsorship §5 User Stories Mapping :14390]; Related: banner placement options on the floor plan (EP-11659, via EP-1675) [MASTER Floor Plan §5 User Stories Mapping :13643]

name: Clear banner aspect ratio format
what: Show banner image aspect ratios in Exhibitor Portal → Sponsorships → Banner Upload as a ratio (e.g. "7.2:1", optionally "36:5") instead of a single number, wherever banner specifications appear.
why: Frankfurter Buchmesse says "Image aspect ratio 7.2" is unclear to exhibitors and designers preparing sponsored banners.
outcome: Exhibitors understand the required banner proportions and upload correctly sized graphics.

name: Invoice retention after account deletion
what: Keep invoice and payment information when the related account is removed with "remove my account globally".
why: Adventics / Frankfurter Buchmesse accountants lose transactions from the platform once an account is deleted.
outcome: Financial records stay available after account deletion.

name: Consistent currency format with cents
what: Always display money amounts with cents during the registration payment process.
why: DLG: amounts are shown sometimes with and sometimes without cents, which confuses users; their accounting department requires cents.
outcome: All amounts in the payment flow show a consistent format with cents.

name: City search and add on the payment step
what: On the payment step, when a company is the payer, remove the "null" region shown for a city newly added during registration (show the city only or require the region), and add search and the ability to add a city to the city box, as in registration.
why: DLG: the payer address can differ from the registration address, but the city list can only be scrolled, new cities cannot be added, and new cities show a "null" region.
outcome: Payers enter or find their city on the payment step without errors.
builtOverlap: Related (EP-9415): state/region and city added to custom select fields; payment step not covered [MASTER Exhibitor Portal §5 User Stories Mapping :11250]

name: Branded downloadable documents
what: Apply the event's Brand 1 and Brand 2 colours to documents users download from the platform, such as the schedule sent by email and the marketplace exhibitor list.
why: The design of downloadable documents is not tied to the organiser's branding. Asked by Frankfurter Buchmesse GmbH (T1).
outcome: Documents users download carry only the event's brand colours.

name: Confidentiality wording in autologin emails
what: Add default wording to the footer of emails that contain autologin links saying the content is confidential and must not be shared.
why: At Vinexposium an exhibitor used a buyer's autologin link to view the buyer's messages and meetings, showing that human error can expose accounts.
outcome: Recipients of autologin emails are warned not to forward them.

name: Copy email templates with all languages
what: When copying an email template from another event, copy all its language versions, not only English.
why: Kortrijk Xpo (Busworld) says re-creating the other languages takes extra time.
outcome: Copied templates arrive with all their languages.

name: HTML import in the email builder
what: Let organisers upload an HTML file or paste HTML code in the email builder.
why: Informa's Smart Events team wants emails to look exactly as designed in Eloqua.
outcome: Organisers send platform emails with their own HTML design.

name: Open admin notification links in a new tab
what: Add a setting when sending an Admin Notification to open its links in the same tab or in a new tab, with a help tooltip.
why: Hyve wants external links in admin notifications to open in a new tab, but all links open in the same window today.
outcome: Recipients open notification links in the way the organiser chose, and external links no longer take them away from the platform.
builtOverlap: Related (EP-1085): admin notifications panel redesign; link behaviour is the ask [MASTER User Engagement §5 User Stories Mapping :9988] via EP-43218

name: Email template import, export and finalisation status
what: Export all email templates of an event (registration, networking messaging, session and exhibitor manual templates) with name, header image, from name, subject, HTML body and language, import updated templates in bulk, and show a status (edited, default, finalised), optionally with a progress overview.
why: DLG Markets has no simple way to check that every template has been finalised, especially per language, so default unbranded emails can go out.
outcome: Organisers review and finalise all templates in every language from one file and see which still need work.

name: Email template builder gallery, shared header and From Name variable

why: DLG Markets admins scroll through an unsorted gallery, insert the same header in every email by hand and re-enter the From Name for each event.
outcome: Admins build consistent email templates faster with fewer manual steps.

name: Select all recipients in admin notifications
what: Add a "Select All" checkbox at the top of the Admin Notifications recipient dropdown that includes every user group (team members, company accounts, visitors, buyers, speakers, moderators, admins, non-logged-in app users).
why: Admins at DWTC must tick each group one by one to notify everyone, which is slow and risks leaving a group out, especially for urgent messages. Tier 1 customers asking: Dubai World Trade Centre DWTC/ DXB Live.
outcome: An admin sends a notification to all user groups with one click.
builtOverlap: Related (EP-13566): audience filters by category, role and others exist; no single select-all option [MASTER User Engagement §5 User Stories Mapping :9995] via EP-45245
